user.title: Breakage Radar
user.description:
Breakage Radar compares the custom integrations installed on this system against a public index of Home Assistant APIs that are scheduled for removal, and tells you which release removes them.

The index is downloaded from {index_url} every 12 hours. Nothing is uploaded and no account is needed.

abort.already_configured: Breakage Radar is already set up.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Breakage Radar is already set up. Only one instance is needed.

init.title: Breakage Radar options
init.description: Integrations breaking inside the alert window get their own repair notification. Everything further out is listed together in one summary, so a deadline a year away doesn't sit in your notifications for months.

data_description.alert_window_days: Home Assistant releases once a month, on the first Wednesday, so each 30 days is roughly one release of warning.

integrations_affected.title: {count} custom {noun} will break in a future release
integrations_affected.description:
{count} installed custom {noun} {verb} Home Assistant APIs that are scheduled for removal. Nothing breaks today. The first deadline is {earliest_due}.

**What breaks, and when**

{schedule}

Each one has to be fixed by whoever maintains it. The useful next step is to check the integration's repository for a newer release, or raise it with the author while there is still time. `sensor.breakage_radar_affected` lists the exact file and line for every finding.

Anything breaking within {window} days gets its own notification instead of being listed here. You can change that in this integration's options.

integration_imminent.title: {domain} breaks in about {days} {day_word}
integration_imminent.description:
Home Assistant {release} removes an API that `{domain}` still uses, and that release is due {due}.

Check the integration's repository for a newer release that fixes it. If there isn't one, consider raising an issue there, or finding a replacement before you upgrade.

This notification clears itself once the integration no longer uses the removed API. The exact file and line are in the details on `sensor.breakage_radar_affected`.

integration_broken.title: {domain} uses an API that was removed in Home Assistant {release}
integration_broken.description:
This system is running Home Assistant {release} or later, and `{domain}` still uses an API that release removed. It is most likely failing right now.

Check the integration's repository for an update. If there isn't one, the integration will need replacing, or you can raise it with the author.

This notification clears itself once the integration no longer uses the removed API. The exact file and line are in the details on `sensor.breakage_radar_affected`.
